evidence: Receiving DO2 discontinuity: 12.20 mg/L at 48.0 h to 5.25 mg/L at 48.2 h (simulated_online_sensor), indicating a step aeration/transfer fault rather than metabolic limitation
Receiving DO2 48.2-52.0 h in 4.2-5.7 mg/L band with downward drift; last value 4.27 mg/L at 52.0 h vs minimum constraint 2.0 mg/L
Source batches show no such dip at ~48-52 h (source-1/2/3 DO2 ~10.4-11.2 mg/L), confirming receiving-side anomaly
Delayed assay P=2.89 g/L at 48.0 h in receiving, comparable to sources at 48.0 h (3.06/3.02/2.98 g/L) - production on track prior to event
allowed_actions bounds: combined = feed 0.8, air 1.15, retaining full product mass unlike stop
submission.rationale: Receiving DO2 suffered a step drop at 48.2 h (12.2 -> 5.25 mg/L) unlike any source batch and has since drifted down to 4.27 mg/L, only ~2.3 mg/L above the 2.0 mg/L floor. This is a supply-side fault with worsening margin; a keep risks an oxygen-constraint violation, while stop yields zero production. Air-only (+15%) may be marginal against a ~65% transfer loss, and feed-only slows production without fixing supply. The combined action (feed x0.8, air x1.15) attacks both oxygen supply and demand, restoring the largest DO2 margin with only a ~20% temporary feed cut and no loss of product mass.
submission.uncertainty: Hidden receiving parameters are unavailable; the magnitude of the underlying aeration fault is unknown, so a 15% air increase plus 20% feed cut may only partially restore DO2 (estimated recovery to roughly 6-8 mg/L rather than the pre-event ~12 mg/L). If DO2 continues to fall toward 2.0 mg/L after the intervention, a stronger feed reduction should be considered at the next review point. Assay lags (4 h) mean any P feedback on the intervention arrives late.

evidence: Receiving DO2 online sensor: 12.20 mg/L at 48.0h dropping to 5.25 mg/L at 48.2h and 4.27 mg/L at 52.0h
Source batches 1-3 maintained DO2 ~9-11 mg/L during 48-52h window, showing divergent receiving behavior
Forward model KEEP: post-decision min DO 1.40 mg/L, 4.8h below 2.0 limit, product mass 183.3 kg
Forward model strong_feed_reduction: min DO 2.22 mg/L, 0h below limit, 231.8 kg product, feasible=true
Forward model combined/increase_air/reduce_feed: min DO 1.74/1.45/1.51 mg/L, all infeasible
Delayed P assays: 0.99 g/L at 36h, 2.89 g/L at 48h — production ongoing but oxygen-limited trajectory
submission.rationale: At t=52h the receiving fermentation's DO2 has crashed (~4.3-5.2 mg/L, falling) versus ~10-11 mg/L in all three source batches at comparable age, indicating oxygen demand exceeding transfer capacity. KEEP is projected to violate the 2.0 mg/L minimum for ~4.8h (min ~1.4 mg/L). Among bounded interventions, strong_feed_reduction (0.6x feed, 1.15x air) is the only action the source-calibrated forward model deems feasible: minimum DO ~2.22 mg/L, zero below-limit hours, and the highest retained product mass (~232 kg vs ~183 kg under KEEP). It directly cuts oxygen demand via the feed while adding transfer capacity, preserving batch production rather than stopping (zero counted production).
submission.uncertainty: The forward model is source-calibrated, not receiving-true; the model's transfer multiplier estimate (0.52) and hidden receiving parameters mean actual DO trajectories may differ. Sensitivity members for strong_feed_reduction: 4/5 feasible, min DO range 1.36-3.13 mg/L, product mass 175-623 kg — so a residual risk of still dipping below 2.0 mg/L in unfavorable realizations. Delayed assay availability (4h lag) limits real-time state knowledge; if DO2 continues falling faster than modeled, further escalation would be warranted.
